pitch_detail.notes: Clean corner taken with hand and finger jams. The steep crux comes early, with an odd ring bolt clipped near it. Past it, angle left up a ramp and build a gear anchor at a convenient spot.
Ledgy ground straight up the buttress to a point where you can either walk off right into the gully or reach the summit by scrambling easier 4th and low 5th terrain.

review.changed: 2 pitches with grades and lengths; no rappels.

pitch_detail.notes: Scrambly ridge on the north side of the peak with many line choices. Protection is available but most parties solo or simul-climb it. Finish in the small alcove at the base of the crack feature.
From the alcove, a few finger-crack moves lead into a short offwidth that ends at a false summit. The true summit is an easy 4th-class scramble on the west side.

review.changed: 2 pitches; no lengths stated. Descent is a downclimb, so no rappel table.

pitch_detail.notes: Starts from a ledge with a bolt about 8 feet up. Moderate ground and a right-sloping ledge, then very easy terrain before cutting left to the anchor.
Climb onto the anchor ledge and angle slightly right to a bolt on a slab, then continue straight up. Skip the first bolt unless linking with pitch 1.

review.changed: 2 pitches with grade, length, bolts. Descent is two raps from a chain anchor 25 ft right; not a station list.

pitch_detail.notes: Crux move right off the ledge, protected by the first bolt; a heel hook can help on the smooth rock. Large holds on moderate ground lead to a short steep section with a few fun moves, then right to the chain anchor.
Climb up and left from the belay to a bolt, then into a small alcove with an enjoyable move past another hanger. Scramble across a ledge to the anchor. Small to medium gear supplements the bolts.

review.changed: 2 pitches. Descent is two rappels to the base; no station detail.

pitch_detail.notes: A steep move gains a ledge, then traverse well left and climb up past a mix of bolts and gear.
Easy climbing trending left.
Bolts and gear protect the final pitch.

review.changed: 3 pitches, thin notes; no lengths.

pitch_detail.notes: Scramble low-angle rock to a ledge, then about 8 feet more to the first clip. Go straight up over two bulges with the crux at the third hanger, continue on enjoyable climbing, then move left at the top to a chain anchor.
From the anchor go up and slightly right to a good crack taking small and medium gear. Two bolts mark the line, so gear is optional on this easy 5th class.

review.changed: 2 pitches. Descent: walk right 50 ft to a chain anchor, two raps; not tabulated.

pitch_detail.notes: Start with an easy scramble up a gentle slope onto a ledge. The first bolt is two or three moves up on big holds. Roughly 50 feet of quality rock follow, and the anchor is a chain station off to the right.
From the belay go up and left across a ledge to a bolt on a bulge, then up a slab with easy scrambling to the anchor.

review.changed: 2 pitches. Descent two raps from chain anchor; not tabulated.

pitch_detail.notes: Scramble low-angle rock past one bolt to a ledge. Clip a hanger 6 feet above it and climb a steep 40-foot section; the upper part eases to scrambling up to the chain anchor.
From the belay go straight up about 20 feet to a bolt. Further 5.7-minus moves and 5th-class scrambling lead to a chain anchor at the cliff top.

review.changed: 2 pitches; second pitch length unit assumed feet. Descent is two raps; not tabulated.

pitch_detail.notes: Starts under a roof; laybacking and stemming over it.
Good finger cracks.
The obvious dihedral.
Rock quality drops off here and on the next pitch.
Continues in poorer rock.
Belay is bolted. The line heads leftward across steep pale rock on finger cracks; fiddly small nuts protect the start just above the belay. A fall just above the belay could be serious.

review.changed: Pitches 1-6 only; further 5.7 pitches to the buttress top and a second buttress are not itemised. Pitches 4 and 5 ungraded.
review.other_findings: Stored 7 pitches; text implies 8 to first buttress top and about 15 overall. Rappel with 2 60m ropes.

pitch_detail.notes: Obvious corner right of El Shaddai. Some years it is dry; when ice forms in the lower pitches it can be climbed with protection in the crack system to the right. Belay is probably bolted or fixed gear.
Continues up the corner; bolted anchor at the top of the pitch, as best remembered.
A long corner that looks like it needs cams up to about 3-4 inches. Grade uncertain; not confirmed.

review.changed: 3 pitches from a hedged account; no lengths.

pitch_detail.notes: Difficult leftward-trending mixed climbing to reach a very thin ice sheet that gradually firms up. Bolts protect the pitch and the belay.
Straight up through steep terrain on more thin ice, ending with a few hard rock moves before the bolted anchor.
A hanging dagger off a roof is climbed directly. Unlike the lower pitches, the belay here is not bolted.

review.changed: 3 pitches. Rappels are bolt-to-bolt single raps but no station list.

pitch_detail.notes: An iced slab opens the climb; ease left and upward until you stand below the main smear. A little moderate mixed ground leads to a large boulder draped in webbing; belay there, out of the line of falling ice.

Moderate ice to a vertical, runout smear with sparse gear and hooking moves. A few small rock pieces may be placeable, mostly near the top. Mantle the snow lip, then about 60 feet higher a fixed pin plus a bolt form the belay on rock.

review.changed: 2 pitches; no per-pitch grades or lengths stated.
review.other_findings: Difficulty varies a lot with conditions (WI4 to WI6).

pitch_detail.notes: Steep corner with ample cracks and moss. Higher up choose straight up the better corner or right on easier but more runout ground.
Powerful pulling on a steep crack that drifts left inside a corner, then over onto neve and up a runnel to a snow ledge below the chockstone feature.
Deceptively long and hard. Moderate corner system up toward the chockstone; steep moves exit to the belay.
Wide corner under a chockstone, awkward winter crack climbing and hooks on loose rock in the back. Move left around the chockstone with poor feet, then an anchor sits up on the right.

review.changed: 4 pitches with grades and lengths.

pitch_detail.notes: Traverse right on low-angle ground to reach the large corner system.
Climb through roofs up the corner.
Continue up the corner.
Regain the corner system, with an offwidth and hand crack. Good pitch.
Finish the corner, go right on a ledge, back up left to a big ledge and belay at a block below the key pitch.
Low-angle cracks steepen to a sweeping roof with stemming and face holds on the right, then up the corner over a second roof to a large ledge.
Go right around a big flake, up blocky ground to the headwall base, then a steep finger crack.
A hard step left from the stance, plus a few awkward moves, gains a ledge. Easier cracks then lead to the foot of the finger crack.
Stem beside the finger crack, then go left on unprotected 5.8 face to a roomy ledge where a rappel anchor sits. A low-angle offwidth and 5- hand cracks lead to the summit.

review.changed: 9 pitches of the original line; alternate start pitches 1a-3a (5.9, 5-, 5-) for a wet corner are not tabulated. No rappel station table.

pitch_detail.notes: Start up a ramp heading left, then steeper terrain to a bolted anchor under a roof.
Shorter and easier; goes out right in a traverse to the second anchor of the neighbouring route. A 4 inch cam helps on the traverse near the top.

review.changed: 2 pitches, no grades or lengths in text.

pitch_detail.notes: One bolt below the ledge, then fun face moves, moving left to a chain anchor.
Leave the anchor angling up and right past two bolts toward a small dihedral against the sky, and finish straight up to the next anchor.

review.changed: 2 pitches. Descent is two raps; not tabulated.

pitch_detail.notes: Wide crack up to the top of a small summit. The crux is about halfway where the crack narrows past a small roof with an old piton. Single bolt anchor; back it up with gear at your feet. Rappel the far side into a tundra bowl.
Cross the bowl to a big chimney and take it with gear in the back; a bit of a grovel. Exit the top and shuffle left to a ledge belay.
Broken ledgy terrain with a few real moves up to the top of the wall. Unrope and walk to the true summit.

review.changed: 3 pitches; no rappel table.

pitch_detail.notes: Low-angle grassy gully at the buttress toe; most parties scramble. The belay is a pair of bolts on the left side of the ramp.

Traverse left on face holds to a dirty corner, then a big left-facing flake toward the large dihedral. Sustained moves with gear that is not always perfect; a left and right variation near the top, both somewhat runout. Hanging belay on finger to hand gear.
Stemming and chimneying up a groove that opens out and gets harder. Protection is good. The corner arches left; hard moves reach a grass ramp with a two-nut anchor.
Traverse beneath the arch, jamming and underclinging left with good but dirty gear, to a grass perch below a left-facing corner. Finger to hand gear belay.
Move left off the belay, clipping a strangely positioned bolt, and pull a steep crux that takes decent gear. Follow the flake and the crack beside it up to a big grassy ledge.
Climb the middle of the small blocky tower trending left to the top. Easy and unremarkable.

review.changed: 6 pitches. Descent is a rap, 4th class and another rap; not tabulated.

pitch_detail.notes: Up the big gully that splits the wall. A few easy moves lead to flared sections and a corner facing right where gear goes deep in the crack. Bring big pieces and watch for loose rock onto your partner.
Continue up the gully over easy sections and a ledge system to a two-bolt anchor. The chain rappel station lies a few metres left and slightly below.

review.changed: 2 pitches without grades or lengths.

pitch_detail.notes: Crux off the ground on a smooth ledge that is slick when wet. Clip the first bolt from the ledge, three more bolts to a good small-to-medium crack, then left to a chain anchor.
From the belay step right and climb straight up past three bolts on enjoyable scrambling to the chain anchor.

review.changed: 2 pitches; second pitch bolt count omitted (header says 2, text says 3). Descent: rappel the route.
